user.text:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

history.assistant:
Built the reading tracker. It has separate “currently reading” and “finished” shelves, a form for adding books, individual book pages with notes, status changes, and a button to copy a book’s direct link. Books are saved in `data/books.json` and remain there after a restart; no accounts or database are needed.

Run `npm start`, then open http://localhost:3000. The JSON file includes five removable example books.

Verification passed: `npm test` (2 tests), `node --check` on the server, store, and client scripts, `npm run build`, and HTTP checks for the home page, book link, assets, and API (all 200). I couldn’t check the visual layout in a browser here.

{"path":"README.md","content":"# Between Pages

A small, account-free reading tracker. Keep a shelf of books you're reading and have finished, add notes, and share a direct link to any book. Everything is saved in a local JSON file.

## Run

Requires Node.js 18 or newer.

```sh
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Set `PORT` to use a different port, for example `PORT=4000 npm start`.

The included `data/books.json` contains five example books so you can explore the app immediately. You can remove them from their detail pages, or replace the file contents with `[]` to start with an empty shelf. New books and changes are saved to this file and remain after restarting the server. Back it up if you want to keep your collection. Run this on a server with a persistent filesystem; ephemeral hosting will not preserve the JSON file across deployments.

## Features

- Add books as currently reading or finished, with optional notes.
- Move books between shelves, edit notes, or remove a book.
- Open a book's own `/books/:id` URL and copy that link to share it. Whoever opens the link needs access to the running app; there are no accounts or private books.
- No database, build tooling, or runtime dependencies.

## Check

```sh
npm test
```
"}

# Between Pages

A small, account-free reading tracker. Keep a shelf of books you're reading and have finished, add notes, and share a direct link to any book. Everything is saved in a local JSON file.

## Run

Requires Node.js 18 or newer.

```sh
npm start
```

Open http://localhost:3000. Set `PORT` to use a different port, for example `PORT=4000 npm start`.

The included `data/books.json` contains five example books so you can explore the app immediately. You can remove them from their detail pages, or replace the file contents with `[]` to start with an empty shelf. New books and changes are saved to this file and remain after restarting the server. Back it up if you want to keep your collection. Run this on a server with a persistent filesystem; ephemeral hosting will not preserve the JSON file across deployments.

## Features

- Add books as currently reading or finished, with optional notes.
- Move books between shelves, edit notes, or remove a book.
- Open a book's own `/books/:id` URL and copy that link to share it. Whoever opens the link needs access to the running app; there are no accounts or private books.
- No database, build tooling, or runtime dependencies.

## Check

```sh
npm test
```
